answer: Cohort-gated admission resists sybils. Identities join only in fixed-size cohorts, each posting a bond priced at c times the cohort index, so marginal cost rises linearly with n: minting N puppets locks cN in capital, each paying the fee once, no batch discount. The identity cipher is bound to this time-locked bond and cannot be reset in parallel: a reset forfeits the escrow and restarts the queue, and payouts settle only after the lock expires, so pre-aged clones are worthless. The escrow pool is the garden: each admission leaves a plume, a receipt auditors prune.
